title: An empty map at the depth limit is admitted where a non-empty map is truncated
rationale: flattenValue checks isEmpty and short-circuits to a null BEFORE ever calling flattenObject, so the depth check never runs for an empty container. The bound is not applied uniformly and the exemption is invisible from the configuration.
catchesBugClass: Non-uniform enforcement of a bound - a guard that a specific value shape can walk around. Also pins that the isEmpty short-circuit ordering is load-bearing.
cannotCatch: With a single empty terminal the exemption costs at most one level, so it cannot demonstrate unbounded bypass. It also cannot distinguish the collapse from the skipped bound by round-trip comparison alone - the flattened map assertion is what names it.

predicted.detail: Two sibling values at the identical structural position, one exempt from the bound and one not: {} becomes null without consulting maxDepth while the non-empty sibling is stringified.
